messages:
nina_sales: Prospect asked for a pared-down artifact list to sign the POC and for clarity on whether we share the full pen-test report or only a redacted summary. They also want to know if reserved/dedicated pricing must be locked before POC. Deadline: COB Wed.

omar_ps: For POCs we typically provide: SOC 2 Type II attestation (or signed controls summary), pen-test attestation letter (signed) or redacted executive summary, a UAT/staging network diagram, SSO/SAML integration notes + one test account, staging IP whitelist (or VPN details), short POC runbook (support hours/escalation), and a data residency statement if applicable.

omar_ps: Reserved/dedicated pricing is NOT required to start a POC. We can run on shared infra. If they want guaranteed throughput/latency we quote a short reserved window but that is optional.

lucy_security: Pen-test policy: default = signed attestation + redacted findings summary. Full/raw reports require NDA + legal approval + secure dataroom access. Attestation includes: scope (external/internal), date, severity summary, and confirmation of no outstanding criticals or remediation ETA for any high findings. We won't share raw scanner logs or vendor PII.

lucy_security: If the buyer's legal insists on full report, ask for the reason and CISO/legal contact. We can prepare a limited-access dataroom; security needs approval and ops support.

ben_ops: For short POCs we can offer ephemeral public ranges (48-hour or 2-week windows). Example firewall snippet they can paste into their firewall:
```
- UAT ingress: 52.23.45.0/29
- Callback endpoints: 52.23.45.8/30
- Admin API (ephemeral): 52.23.45.13
```
Static/public IPs for month-long windows are possible but require ~72 hours lead time and may trigger reserved infra charges.

nina_sales: Can someone convert this to a one-page acceptance checklist I can email? Buyer asked: "If we hand over network diagram + SSO + pen-test letter, is that normally enough to sign off?"

omar_ps: Usually yes if the pen-test attestation states no open criticals and the SSO flow is validated end-to-end in staging. Here's a concise one-page acceptance checklist you can send them:
- SOC 2 Type II attestation OR signed controls summary
- Penetration test attestation (signed) OR redacted executive summary (statement of no open criticals + remediation ETA for any high findings)
- Network architecture diagram for UAT/staging (include any on-prem connectors)
- SSO/SAML test user successfully authenticated in staging
- Confirmation of staging IP whitelist or VPN connection details
- POC support hours and escalation contact (include pager/email)
- If required by buyer: KMS/HSM key custody statement or integration note

omar_ps: Add a line: "Full pen-test report available under NDA in secure dataroom; request legal/CISO contact."

lucy_security: I'll attach our pen-test attestation template and can redline if their legal requests changes. Security will sign the technical attestation; legal should sign any contractual addendum.

ben_ops: Ping me if they want static IPs or a month-long reserved window and i'll open the ops ticket (3 business days lead).

nina_sales: Great — i'll send the checklist and ask whether they want redacted summary or full report. i'll capture their legal/CISO and loop you in if they push for full disclosure or dedicated pricing. thanks! :thumbsup:
